practiceReport.name: Denzel Ward
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (9th NFL season, 99% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
practiceReport.beatComment: Ward was managing a quad injury during all of Week 10 prep, but he avoided an injury tag for Sunday's game despite not logging a full practice. The veteran defensive back has 34 tackles (19 solo), nine pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.

practiceReport.name: Quincy Williams
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (8th NFL season, 96% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
practiceReport.beatComment: Williams has had his practice reps over the last couple of weeks limited while tending to a hamstring injury, but he has yet to miss a regular-season game, and that trend will continue for Sunday's home tilt. The veteran linebacker has accumulated 62 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and four forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.

practiceReport.name: Denzel Boston
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (90% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

practiceReport.name: Derek Barnett
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Barnett left in the first quarter due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran defensive lineman was cleared by medical staff to return to Sunday's contest.

irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: 21-day practice window opened; eligible for 53-man roster activation (Quadriceps).

irAndReserveTracker.name: Raheim Sanders
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Cleveland elected to open Sanders' practice window following their Week 11 bye, giving the team up to 21 days to evaluate him for a return to the 53-man roster. Before landing on IR on Oct. 13 due to a hip issue, Sanders carried nine times for 43 yards and added 11 receptions for 74 yards on 12 targets over five contests. He'll likely slot in behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson on the depth chart at running back once he's activated.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Michael Burton
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 11 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.
